Selection of any particular method of depth measurement depends on depth of flow, velocity of For example, wading rods are used when current and the method of discharge observation. velocities are low, say, 1 m/s and depths are small and wadable, say, up to 1 m; sounding rods are used for velocities upto 2 m/s and depths say, up to 5 m and hand lines with weights are used for still greater depths and velocities. This standard was first published in 1966. This revision has been prepared to incorporate the latest practice in the field and the use of materials like hollow steel section or aluminium pipe iIp the manufacture of such rods.

.l SCOPE This standard covers the functional requirements and tests for performance of sounding rods. It also covers the materials to be used for their manufacture. 2 REFERENCES For the purpose of this standard definitions given in IS 1191 : 1971 `Glossary of terms and symbols used in connection with the measurement of liquid flow with a free surface ( first revision )' shall apply. 3 FUNCTIONAL Each sounding requirements: REQUIREMENTS rod shall satisfy the following the field, on three sounding rods for every 24 of identical shape, size and dimensions.
in

4.1.1 The rod shall not penetrate more than 5 mm into a bed of 0'3 m depth of the same material as of the channel in which it is to be used, under a vertically applied pressure of 50 kg ( in addition to its own weight ). 4.1.2 When the rod is simply supported over a span equal to the length of the rod and subjected to a central concentrated load of 20 kg, the maximum deflection should not exceed 5 mm. 4.1.3 The sounding rod should have astreamlined section so as to cause minimum heading up of water which shall not exceed 2 percent of the depth of flow. NOTE - If the limit is exceeded then other
methods to. 5 of depth measurement should be resorted

a) Its mass should be as low as possible; b) It should be straight and have sufficient strength to withstand the force due without signilicant to flowing water deflection or vibration. It may be sectional to allow it to be dismantled. The sectional connection should not interfere with positioning or operation of the current metre; c) Construction should resistant material; of be of corrosion

ANNEX A ( Clause 5.1 )
TYPICAL A-l GENERAL Sounding rods are broadly classified into 2 groups namely, a) sounding rods for depths up to 2 and 3 m; and b) sounding rods for depths up to 6 m. Although both types of sounding rods are made of steel, aluminium and wood, longer sounding rods may alss be made of bamboo for lightness in weight. A-2 WOODEN SOUNDING RODS DETAILS OF SOUNDING RODS

A-2.1 The sounding rods shall be made of strong, completely seasoned wcod, oval in shape and very smooth over its entire surfaces. It shall consist of the following parts:

Threads should be provided in the nipple and flange and the former should be screwed securely to the latter. The entire length of the nipple should receive the circular bottom portion of the sounding rod for perfect rigidity. The flange plate may be perforated at its per-iphery. The bottom of the circular rod and nipple should be connected with screws. On the top of the rod, a plumb ball should be provided to ensure its verticality and a rope should be attached to the nipple to keep it reasonably vertical when the flow is rapid. Figure 1 gives the details. A-3 BAMBOO SOUNDING RODS

A-2.2 Details A-2.2.1 Oval Shaped Wooden Rod The size of the oval shaped wooden rod should be about 80 mm X 20 mm, they should be 2 or 3 m long and smooth along their entire surface. It shall be graduated in metres, decimetres and centimetres with enamel paint or by etching and painting them with white and black paint. The numbers in metres and decimeters and their graduations should be marked conspicuously in red enamel paint. A-2.2.2 Metallic
Nipple Circulur Base Plate with

A-3.1 Bamboos may also be used for sounding in depths upto 6 m. These are reasonably strong and lighter to use as compared to solid wooden rods. When bamboo is proposed to be used care should be taken to select a long, straight and strong bamboo of adequate girth, say, about 40 mm diameter. The bamboo should not be green and/or cracked. It should be correctly and clearly marked with enamel paint like the wooden oval shaped sounding rod. It should also be provided with a 100 mm diameter circular base plate with a flange to hold the bamboo rod in the same way as the oval shaped' wooden rod is fixed to its base. Figure 1 gives the details. A-4 STEEL/ALUMINIUM SOUNDING RODS

It shall consist of a metallic disc approximately 150 mm in diameter and 5 mm thick having a circular flange with an opening of about 80 mm diameter to engage a nipple of the same size.

A-4.1 Steel/Aluminium pipes may be used for sounding in depths up to 4 m. These are made of steel or aluminium pipe with an outer diameter of 20 mm. These shall be graduated in metres decimetres and centimetres by engraving. The rods are made up of I m lengths that can be joined together by threaded joints. Base plate of steel, 100 mm in diameter and 10 mm thick is also fixed to the rod by threads. A sliding support is provided for fixing the current meter at the desired depths.

Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'.
